stories.title: RSS globalised: Inside the Hindu nationalist paramilitary leader's carefully staged NYC celebration of ‘universal oneness’
stories.summary: Madison Square Garden, the legendary artistic centre of New York City and a global stage for major sports and entertainment for more than 140 years, is widely regarded as the world’s most famous arena. On Saturday afternoon, however, the event space was home to an audience that did not quite resemble Harry Styles concert-goers or Knicks fans. Crowds of Indian and Hindu Americans of all ages, clad in bright saffron caps, kurtas, and saris, arrived from across the country to see Mohan Bhagwat, the chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a Hindu nationalist paramilitary group, whose affiliate organisations are driving violence against minorities in India. Hosted by American Hindus for Engagement And Dialogue (Ahead), Saturday’s "Universal Oneness Celebration" presented itself as "an afternoon of shared teaching, cultural performance, and common ground". I attended the event as a correspondent for Middle East Eye on Saturday. What I witnessed was a careful repackaging of an entity described by critics as the "world’s largest fascist organisation" into the language of inclusion and pluralism, as escalating communal violence in India continues to claim lives daily. Formed in 1925, the RSS is a Hindu nationalist organisation with more than five million members across the world, to advance the vision of Hindutva: a political project that seeks to establish India as a homogenous, Hindu ethnostate. One of its primary ideological progenitors, MS Golwalkar, looked towards Nazi Germany’s ethnic cleansing of European Jews as "a good lesson for us in Hindustan to learn and profit by", referring to India’s Muslims. Likewise, VD Savarkar, regarded as the founder of the exclusionary ideology of Hindutva, viewed the Zionist project in Palestine as a model for India to embody. India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party was born out of the RSS’s ideological family, the Sangh Parivar and most of its leading members, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, are members of the organisation. Senior BJP leaders, including cabinet ministers, have openly called for the killing of India's Muslims in hate speeches, referring to them as "green snakes". Despite its "universal" branding, prospective attendees had to undergo identity-based vetting to attend the free event.

stories.summary: Michael Pettis says a great rebalancing is coming and China will pay for it. It’s strange how the man who insists that power decides who pays never tests his claim on Washington.
